I still remember when I saw the trailer for this game while I was having dinner at Hooters with my family, back in 2011. It was actually then that I told my parents that if they wanted to give me something for my birthday, which was coming up in two weeks or so, that game would be it. I was absolutely mesmerized at the time—as I am still now–so you couldn’t convince me to want a unicorn, a million dollars, or anything else that wasn’t this game.
As a kid, I was used to playing videogames on ps2, Gamecube, N64, all kinds of handhelds, etc., so when my birthday came up and my parents had actually gifted me my very first "modern" console, being the Xbox360, you can imagine how excited I was. To top it off, this very game was taped right on my new Xbox; I can literally still smell the fresh plastic that was wrapping the game. This game marked a huge stepping point in my gaming timeline; a step I would remember and cherish for the years to come.
MW3 was the first CoD that I owned that had an active multiplayer, because as much as I played on the predecessors of Xbox360 and ps3, the servers on these older consoles weren't exactly appealing or simple to use—and therefore, enjoy. Back then also MW2 was the main vibe and every one of my friends were playing it, but my parents refused to let me have a console because they had the old-school mentality that videogames were bad for you and whatnot. So again, my birthday came up, and what had been an allusion for many years became a reality—I was finally able to be part of the cool kids! 
When my best friend found out I got an Xbox 360 with this game, he was as excited as I was because he claimed he didn't have anyone to play with before and now he would. At the time, I was overwhelmingly happy to get a console, plus I was used to playing by myself, so I didn't really think much of this.  
We played every. single. day. – literally. As soon as we got out of school, he or I would text the other and we would get online and play. We sorta became CoD freaks. Sometimes I would go to his house and we would split-screen a few rounds of Zombies. He was really good; like, he was the kind of kid to achieve prestige within freaking hours of getting the game. It is needless to state that he was always carrying me… 
I was already in love with the CoD franchise because I really enjoyed playing war games, so when I was able to enter the multiplayer world, with my best friend, it was mind-blowing, to say the least. I continued playing with him all throughout high school, up until we graduated in 2014 and we each went to our respective colleges. As college students, we didn’t play as frequently–for obvious reasons–but we would still play at least once a week, if we were able to. I stayed home for college, but he went out-of-state, so gaming became even more meaningful for us because we were not seeing each other physically anymore. 
My best friend had a heart condition, and in 2017, he had to undergo surgery; it was something he had to do every few months, so he was practically used to it. The surgery went well, and after it was done, it was procedural to just wait for him to wake up from the anesthesia. 
The morning following the surgery, at precisely 5:08am, I was woken up by a text from my best friend’s sister letting me know he had passed away. I remember I didn’t reply, and I simply got out of bed to go to work. I was completely and utterly numb, feeling nothing, absolutely nothing. I remember I didn’t cry at all that day; not a single tear. I carried on with my day, as if nothing had happened. 
It didn’t hit me until I had to tell my parents, who were out of town at the time. I called them the following morning, and I told them. As soon as I said, "He's gone, mom," I could hear my dad rapidly pulling over, and I could sense my mom was starting to cry. She was stunned, literally, too stunned to speak. And all that follows you can already imagine. 
When I was walking away from that stage after getting my high school diploma, I never expected I would have to say goodbye to my best friend forever just three years after. Months before, we had literally just celebrated that he turned 21 and we were joking as we were envisioning what else awaited our futures–if only we had known. 
I stopped playing MW3 after that, and pretty much all of the CoD multiplayers. Not because I was undergoing a sort of denial, but rather because life kept going on and my gaming interests had to be placed aside a little–I was, after all, still a college student. 
And yes, as I had foreseen, life carried on. I sold most of my consoles as time went by because I got tired of carrying them everywhere and all. The Xbox360 servers eventually shut down, and I got rid of all my games, but my console is still with me, although it honestly just serves as a memento. Eventually I entered the world of pc gaming, and all consoles were pretty much obsolete for me. As I finished college, I started playing the more mainstream games, such as Fortnite, Rocket League, and of course, CoD. I never quite got around to appreciating Warzone because of many things I won’t describe here, but I know he would’ve loved it, and I know that just as he was alongside me with MW3, we would have been ceaselessly making people rage in Warzone—or at least he would’ve. Maybe that’s why I’m indifferent towards the game, and for that bias, I apologize. 
What I won’t apologize for is writing this “review.” What do you want me to say? I have already stated how amazing this game is without having to address it in the remotest of chances. This game gave me countless of memories alongside my best friend, and while I may never again find another person to share these kinds of memories the same way I did with him, my gratitude remains with CoD for giving us so, so, SO much. This game was, and is, perfect. I don’t care what gamers say about MW2 being the best one, in my eyes they’re wrong–this is it, this is the best CoD has given us. 
So thank you for “Infected,” for allowing us to get back at Makarov, and for adding the Terminal map as we expected back when it was still cool. Again, there are no additions, no corrections, no changes I would make. This was it, Activision–this was your peak. Thank you. 
I realized two days ago that CoD games were on Steam, and to make it even better, they were discounted; so, naturally, I obliged, bought them all, and started making my way through this campaign first. And just as I was thrilled back then, I am still now, despite of the fact that a huge piece of my initial experience is missing. 
So if you’re thinking of buying this game, stop–just do it already. I can’t assure it will give you as much as it has given me, but I have a feeling you’re going to love it perhaps as much as I do. Least you can do is try. 

This is dedicated to all those players that have gone ‘offline’ forever. Your status will always remain ‘online’ in our hearts.

In memory of my best friend—rest in peace, Dante.

Modern Warfare 3 is the most underrated Call of Duty of all time. 
The reason people at the time weren't as excited about this game was because of the similarities to Modern Warfare 2, but if you hadn't played that previously, and you came in when this game released, chances are, you would think Modern Warfare 3 was awesome. 
Especially seeing as to where Call of Duty as a franchise is now, I'd say that this game has been better than almost every other Call of Duty title made post Black Ops 2.
It is great to see that in retrospect, more and more people are showing this game the love it deserves. It had a very satisfying ending to the Modern Warfare series campaign, Spec Ops and Survival were very fun and re-playable (this is coming from a veteran zombies player), and the Multiplayer is among my all time favorites along with the other elites, which in my opinion are the first two Black Ops games and Modern Warfare 2. Combined with my Steam account and my old PS3 account, I probably have close to 1,000 hours played on Modern Warfare 3. For me, the game was very re-playable with all of the guns available, the perks, the prestiging, and playing Survival with friends and trying constantly to get to level 50 because we sucked haha.
The only complaint I really have about this game now, is that Multiplayer in 2022 is basically dead/unplayable because no one really plays the multiplayer anymore. If your lucky enough to find a game, which it will probably be Team Death match, you won't get any hackers in your game. However in my experience, it is basically a 50/50 shot. 
During the beginning of quarantine in early 2020, hackers were much rarer because there were tons of players coming back to play the game for a period of time, which was a very memorable and great experience.
If you still want to play the Multiplayer, I'd highly recommend getting the Plutonium IW5 mod so that way you can play on servers with other players and not have to worry about hackers and other stuff.
Despite being initially disliked at launch, I think nowadays most people would agree that Modern Warfare 3 was a damn good game. Seeing where COD is now, this game is light years ahead of the GARBAGE we have now *cough *Vanguard *cough. If they ever remastered Modern Warfare 2 and Modern Warfare 3 with a multiplayer, I don't think I'd need to buy a new Call of Duty ever again (except for a Black Ops 2 remaster LOL).
My final rating for Modern Warfare 3 is a 8/10. If multiplayer was still alive, I'd pry give it a 9/10.

[h1] DO NOT PURCHASE, UNSAFE TO PLAY [/h1]

Activision charges $90 for this dead game, most of which can't even be played due to major netcode problems. It's only $40 if you don't buy the DLC, but then you're left with almost zero content and can no longer 100% the game, because unlike previous titles, this game comes with multiple achievements that are DLC-exclusive. Either way, you're getting massively screwed.

As mentioned in a previous review, several legacy Call of Duty games have multiple security vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2018-20817. This allows hackers to gain direct control of your PC via Remote Code Executions, which could allow them to access, add, or remove any files to and from your PC. That means an unsuspecting player can buy this game, go play a single round of team deathmatch, and have all of their personal documents, passwords, and accounts stolen, not knowing a thing until it's too late. 
This issue has been well documented by programmers and researchers, and a simple internet search will reveal that it has affected countless Steam players. However, Activision refuses to fix it, and does not provide any customer support for players affected.

Due to backwards compatibility and recent matchmaking fixes, servers for legacy COD games on console are well populated. I've seen unofficial PC clients with even higher player counts, with Discord servers reaching hundreds of thousands of members. It's obvious that people miss old COD, but Activision has put more effort into sending cease and desist letters to free fan-made clients, than they have into fixing the games that made Call of Duty into an industry titan.

If Activision is going to continue selling these titles at full price without fixing major security flaws, or at least disabling multiplayer functions, then Steam needs to remove these titles from sale. I hope it doesn't get to that point, but players deserve better,

The last great single player Call of Duty game in the last great Call of Duty series (Modern Warfare Trilogy). The story picks up where we left off in Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2 so if you haven't played that before there is no point in playing this game however if you're here after playing the prequel and want to know if the sequel is worth it then yes it is. Not only is the sequel good it surpasses the prequel MW2 in many ways. You'll have a great time playing this if you enjoyed COD MW,MW2. But as is the issue with all other COD games this one is also EXTREMELY OVERPRICED for it's age. So buy it only on sale.

Note: This review is coming from someone who played the singleplayer only and not the multiplayer since this game doesn't have many people playing left.

Cod MW3 is the third and final installment in the original MW storyline. Its campaign is just as good the previous installments and its Survival mode makes it much more replayable. Even if its graphics have aged with time its gameplay is just as good as triple a shooters these days.  

Graphics (7/10) The game's graphics are pretty dated so if you're all about graphics you won't like this. Personally I think the old and dirty aesthetic of the graphics helps compliment the game's dark depiction of war and terrorism. It also helps make the game easier to run for lower end pcs.

Gameplay (8/10) The gameplay is still satisfying and the game gives a large amount of weapons and gadgets to mess around with. Though it does feel very similar to Cod MW2 since its arsenal is mostly the same. Enemies aren't too easy or hard as they will take cover and take turns shooting but they don't have laser accuracy and are balanced. The veteran mode of the campaign also doesn't feel too hard or easy which is good if you're not a dorito snorting tryhard. 

Survival Mode (10/10) The newly introduced Survival mode for MW3 is absolutely awesome and this feature alone makes the game worth it. Surviving endless waves of enemies in huge maps with lots of weapons and assets to choose from. The enemy will swarm you from every direction and the maps have lots of space making sure that every area has at least 3 routes. The weapons and killstreaks from the multiplayer return here. You can even get friendly ai to fight alongside you. The only problem I have with the ai is they follow you no matter what which can be annoying if you setup defenses then run across the map to buy ammo but they follow you out. It would have also been cool if allies were accurate with the setting like PMC soldiers for Sierra Leone maps. It would also be great if Overlord wasn't the only announcer for this mode. I like the enemies getting tougher with every wave its not too easy or too hard to handle as they get better weapons, body armor, tactics and equipment like dogs, juggernauts and claymore experts to balance your power. The map selection is very diverse from the streets of Paris to the Slums of Sierra Leone to the Mountains of Siberia and classic multiplayer maps like Terminal. The insane maps also help ramp up the difficulty if you thought it was too easy by throwing ground troops, juggernauts and helicopters at you all at once and I love it. Don't forget you can bring a friend with you in survival! You guys will kill together, spam flashbangs on juggernauts together and die together; a good game to play with your bestie.

Spec Ops (10/10) Spec Ops also returns better then ever with new diverse missions. My personal favorite is one where you play as Makarov's goons on the president's plane opposite of where you start in the campaign's mission. This mode is a good way to challenge yourself or want just a quick burst of action. Just like with survival you can bring a friend with you here. Though some of the mission specifically require you to have a friend (if only all my friend's weren't broke as fuck) The dlc missions are especially fun as they introduce some characters that got barely any screentime like Baseplate (Macmillan).

Story (9/10) The story is a very good finale to the MW trilogy as it ties up all loose ends and ends the war. The way information is presented during the mission briefings are quite satisfying. I like the diversity in world settings from New York to Germany to Somalia. I think this game's story is very underrated especially with Delta Force since they don't get as much recognition unlike the Army Rangers from MW2. Delta team in this game is one of my favorite factions in any video game especially because their announcer's voice (Overlord) is so satisfying to hear. Many people tend to overlook all the missions in this game but each one is memorable and distinct. You can really tell the people who made this game made it with love. The only complaint I have for the campaign is the Michael Bay level amount of explosions and repitition of previous mechanics (AC 130 mission, 50 cal sniper mission and machine gun turret section). I'm fine with explosion going of around you as you run but I hate it when the screen is constantly shaking it hurts my head and I get dizzy after only a while of playing.

Multiplayer (?/10) I'm giving this one a question mark because I haven't been able to play it. If you're buying this game for its multiplayer I regret to inform you that not many people play this game anymore. More or less than 500 play this game these days so the chance of finding a public lobby is slim. I couldn't even find a single lobby (maybe cause my internet is crap). I also heard even if you do get a lobby its filled with hackers. Though if you have a friend you could just play face off 1v1 which could be some fun. One thing I do like about the multiplayer is it has different factions unlike the newer cod games with boring team names like "my team" and "enemy team". I also like the different announcers and themes it really makes each faction feel unique and have different goals and personality. I love hearing the GIGN announcer say "servitas vitae". If only the newer cod games like Vanguard were like this and not just the same generic dude for every team who sounds like he's trying to mimic the Halo announcer's charm. Call of Duty when this came out had a soul it wasn't just a lifeless money printer when the devs realized that people will just buy their products even if they sucked. Sad I wasn't able to play this game back in its day but at least I get a glimpse of its awesomeness.  

Map Design (10/10) All of the maps in MW3 are unique, memorable and spacious. I like how big the maps are and their variance of areas like tight corridors, wide open areas, high ground advantages and flanks. This is especially noticeable in Survival as it opens the possibilities to hundreds of spots to hold out, defend or retreat to. The maps are designed so that almost all areas have at least one escape route in case you need to fall back. The vanilla maps are quite gritty, dark and mostly take place in abandoned towns and city skirmishes. I personally really like the city maps as you can hear the ambience of distant gunfire, sirens in the distance and miniguns filling the air with tracer rounds. The dlc maps however are more colorful since they seem to take place in more exotic areas like Central Park in NYC and a seaside retreat somewhere in Italy. 

Music (10/10) Love the music of this game from the frantic music as you run to the rock and roll music as you mow down enemies running from cover. The music in stealth portions also help the gritty tone of the missions as you witness people getting executed or enemies shooting innocent civvies. The menu musics are also bangers as they sound quite intense, bombastic and terrifying hyping you up to play. The spawn themes in the multiplayer are awesome especially since each faction has a different spawn, victory and defeat theme. The rank up guitar riff is satisfying as expected and the challenge complete jingle is also really cool(no idea how they made it but props to the sound designers).

Bugs? I did not encounter any bugs playing in campaign and spec ops.

Pc requirements? If your potato pc can't handle it just turn down the texture quality and it should run smoothly. 

Price? Wait for it to go on sale. Yes this game is good but 16 dollars? that's not worth it. Also the dlc of this game is pretty overpriced considering it only adds a few maps(though they look beautiful.

Conclusion: I give this game a definitive 10/10 lots of replayability and fun. Now I only need to get one of my friend's to purchase this game when it's on sale so we can bro down and go down in survival mode

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 is one of the best classic games in the Call of Duty series. Earlier Modern Warfare games were known for strong impact and high popularity, and this one continues in the same direction without changing the formula much. It still comes as a polished entry with a lot of content. I first played it on Nintendo Wii more than 12 years ago after importing the original disc from the USA, so it also connects with old personal memory.

The campaign continues after the previous game and begins right after it. It moves through different action-heavy missions with varied situations like large battles, close combat sections, and action scenes that are heavily scripted. The story has a few twists and stays serious most of the time. The level design is mostly linear, but it keeps the pacing steady without long breaks.

Multiplayer is a major part of the game. The maps include small close-range maps and larger ones that suit different play styles. The shooting system is similar to earlier entries and does not change much, but it is stable and responsive. I am not much into COD multiplayer because I bought these games mainly for the campaign, but it is still well built and has a lot of content. Co-op modes like Spec Ops and Survival also add extra content, with Survival focusing on wave-based combat and resource management.

I am mentioning this in most of COD reviews, even if there are nice COD games with great campaigns or very good campaigns, the campaign is still short compared to the price being paid even on sale for most CODs, and even now the game or its key is often priced higher than expected for its length, with retail key pricing also being same or more. I also thought about playing Call of Duty: Black Ops before this game, but as of that time it was not on sale, so I played this first since it is a direct continuation of the Modern Warfare series.

In conclusion, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 is a solid entry with a large amount of content across campaign, multiplayer, and co-op. It does not introduce major changes, but it keeps consistent gameplay quality throughout.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 – The End of an Era

If MW1 lit the fuse and MW2 blew everything sky-high, then MW3 is the thunderous finale where the whole world burns — and you’re the poor soul told to clean it up with an assault rifle and a lot of grenades.

Campaign?

Pure cinematic chaos. New York under siege, Paris collapsing, London exploding — this isn’t a war, it’s World War Michael Bay.

Captain Price chain-smoking his way through World War III while growling wisdom in your ear = peak storytelling.

Yes, Soap… we still miss you.

The finale? Soap’s legacy, Price’s revenge, and the kind of ending that makes you sit in silence as the credits roll.

Multiplayer?

Imagine MW2… but caffeinated.

Sleeker, faster, and more balanced (sometimes).

Specialist Strike Package turned average players into temporary gods.

Drop Zone and Kill Confirmed? Genius.

Also, who can forget the classic: “Final Stand” ruining friendships one last time.

Spec Ops & Survival Mode?

Coop missions returned, but Survival stole the show.

Wave after wave of enemies, juggernauts stomping toward you, riot shield squads making you cry.

It was addictive chaos, and the grind to survive “just one more wave” ate entire weekends.

Legacy?
MW3 didn’t reinvent the wheel — it perfectly wrapped up the trilogy that defined a generation.
It’s the end of an arc, the last chapter in the saga of Soap, Ghost (RIP), and Price.
And honestly? Few games have ever felt this final.

Final Verdict:
Modern Warfare 3 is more than just a shooter. It’s the closing chapter of the FPS trilogy that shaped gaming culture forever.
Explosions, betrayal, survival, and Captain Price’s mustache — what else could you want?
